Present value of a series of cash flows

Source: R/4_financialFunctions.R
presentValue.Rd

Evaluate the present value, or the actuarial present value when occurrence probabilities are supplied, of a vector of cash flows discounted at a given set of interest rates. This is the computational kernel on top of which the actuarial APV machinery (Axn, axn, Exn, IAxn, DAxn, ...) is built.

Usage

presentValue(cashFlows, timeIds, interestRates, probabilities, power = 1)

Arguments

cashFlows

Numeric vector of cash flows, coherent in length with timeIds.

timeIds

Numeric vector of time points at which the cashFlows are due.

interestRates

Either a scalar effective interest rate or a numeric vector of the same length as timeIds: entry j discounts the j-th cash flow back to time 0.

probabilities

Optional numeric vector of occurrence probabilities, one per element of cashFlows. If missing a vector of 1's (certainty) is assumed, which turns the output into a plain financial present value.

power

Numeric exponent applied to each discounted (and probability-weighted) cash flow before summation. The default 1 returns a plain APV; higher integer powers are used by the package to compute higher moments of the present value, hence the name.

Value

A numeric scalar: the (actuarial) present value of the cash-flow series.

Details

With power = 1, the function implements $$\mathrm{APV} = \sum_j (1 + i_j)^{-t_j}\, CF_j\, p_j,$$ where (t_j, CF_j, i_j, p_j) are the aligned entries of timeIds, cashFlows, interestRates and probabilities. A missing timeIds is interpreted as the single time \(t = 1\) (a warning is emitted so that silent misalignments can be caught). The numerical work is delegated to the C++ kernel .presentValueC() for performance.

Note

This simple function is the kernel on which the package's actuarial and financial mathematics rest.

References

Broverman, S.A. (2008). Mathematics of Investment and Credit (Fourth Edition), ACTEX Publications.

See also

annuity, Axn, axn

Author

Giorgio A. Spedicato

Examples

# Three $10 payments at the end of years 1-3, certainty, flat 3% rate:
cf <- c(10, 10, 10)
t  <- c(1, 2, 3)
p  <- c(1, 1, 1)
presentValue(cashFlows = cf, timeIds = t, interestRates = 0.03,
             probabilities = p)
#> [1] 28.28611
